reason: The hypothesis relies on premises about coating feasibility, interfacial bonding, and mechanical improvement, but the cited evidence only loosely supports these. E1 discusses PVD as a limited technique and does not demonstrate HEA coatings on W particles. E2 shows improved bonding and mechanical properties for a different system (HEA/diamond) with a different coating (Ti/Ni), not a refractory HEA nanolayer on W. The specific claims about thermal boundary resistance reduction and irradiation resistance are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: A refractory HEA nanolayer can be deposited on particles via PVD
A refractory HEA coating improves interfacial bonding in a composite
Improved interfacial bonding enhances mechanical properties
A Cr–Fe–Ti–Ta HEA is suitable for fusion applications
Reduced thermal boundary resistance increases overall thermal conductivity
